audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Judean advantage, Divine faithfulness, universal accountability, Law's function, righteousness/justice through trust, grace, redemption, hilasterion, boasting excluded.

verses.restored: What then is the advantage of the Judean, or what is the profit of circumcision?

familiar.text: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?

verses.restored: Much in every way. First indeed, that they were entrusted with the oracles of the Divine.

familiar.text: Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.

verses.restored: For what if some were untrusting? Will their untrust nullify the trustworthiness of the Divine?

familiar.text: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?

verses.restored: May it not be. Let the Divine be true though every human be false, just as it is written: So that you may be made righteous/just in your words and prevail when you are judged.

familiar.text: God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.

verses.restored: But if our injustice commends the righteousness/justice of the Divine, what shall we say? Is the Divine unjust to bring wrath? I speak according to human reasoning.

familiar.text: But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who taketh vengeance? (I speak as a man)

verses.restored: May it not be. Otherwise how will the Divine judge the world?

familiar.text: God forbid: for then how shall God judge the world?

verses.restored: But if the truth of the Divine abounded in my falsehood to his glory, why am I still judged as sinner/misaligned?

familiar.text: For if the truth of God hath more abounded through my lie unto his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?

verses.restored: And why not say, as we are slandered and as some claim we say, Let us do harmful things so good may come? Their judgment is just.

familiar.text: And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.

verses.restored: What then? Are we better off? Not entirely; for we have already charged that both Judeans and Greeks are all under sin/misalignment,

familiar.text: What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin;

verses.restored: just as it is written: There is none righteous/just, not even one;

familiar.text: As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:

verses.restored: there is none understanding; there is none seeking out the Divine.

familiar.text: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.

verses.restored: All turned aside; together they became useless; there is none doing kindness, there is not even one.

familiar.text: They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.

verses.restored: Their throat is an opened grave; with their tongues they deceived; venom of asps is under their lips.

familiar.text: Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips:

verses.restored: Their mouth is full of curse and bitterness.

familiar.text: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:

verses.restored: Their feet are swift to pour out blood;

familiar.text: Their feet are swift to shed blood:

verses.restored: ruin and misery are in their ways,

familiar.text: Destruction and misery are in their ways:

verses.restored: and the way of peace they did not know.

familiar.text: And the way of peace have they not known:

verses.restored: There is no reverence of the Divine before their eyes.

familiar.text: There is no fear of God before their eyes.

verses.restored: Now we know that whatever the Law says, it speaks to those in the Law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may become accountable to the Divine.

familiar.text: Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.

verses.restored: Because from works of Law no flesh will be made righteous/just before him; for through Law comes knowledge of sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.

verses.restored: But now, apart from Law, righteousness/justice of the Divine has been manifested, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets,

familiar.text: But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;

verses.restored: righteousness/justice of the Divine through trust of Jesus Messiah for all who trust. For there is no distinction,

familiar.text: Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:

verses.restored: for all sinned/misaligned and fall short of the glory of the Divine,

familiar.text: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;

verses.restored: being made righteous/just freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Messiah Jesus,

familiar.text: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:

verses.restored: whom the Divine set forth as mercy-seat/atoning sign through trust in his blood, for showing his righteousness/justice because of the passing over of former sins/misalignments in the restraint of the Divine,

familiar.text: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;

verses.restored: for showing his righteousness/justice in the present time, so that he might be just and the one making righteous/just the one from the trust of Jesus.

familiar.text: To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.

verses.restored: Where then is boasting? It is excluded. Through what law? Of works? No, but through law of trust.

familiar.text: Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.

verses.restored: For we calculate that a human is made righteous/just by trust apart from works of Law.

familiar.text: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.

verses.restored: Or is the Divine of Judeans only? Is he not also of nations? Yes, also of nations,

familiar.text: Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also:

verses.restored: since the Divine is one, who will make righteous/just circumcision from trust and uncircumcision through trust.

familiar.text: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.

verses.restored: Do we then nullify Law through trust? May it not be; rather, we establish Law.

familiar.text: Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.

translation_notes: The phrase in 3:22 and 3:26 may be heard as trust in Jesus Messiah and/or the trust/faithfulness of Jesus Messiah. The restored wording preserves the genitive ambiguity where possible.
Hilasterion in 3:25 is rendered mercy-seat/atoning sign to avoid flattening complex temple imagery into a single later theory.
